en: The *Buddha-bhāṣita-dhāraṇī-pātra-sūtra*, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with...
There was a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and ten thousand bodhisattvas.
At that time, [a world-system] one hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of buddha-fields away from this buddha-field...

Passing through that many buddha-fields, there is a world-system named Ānandakuñjara (in the Jin language, Huaji—Flower Accumulation). That Buddha is named Ikāpatirāja (in the Jin language, Zuishang Tianwang—Supreme Heavenly King), the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Now, at present, I have dispatched two bodhisattvas:

the first is named Amitābha Dharma (in the Jin language, "Immeasurable Radiance"), and the second is named Mahābha Dharma (in the Jin language, "Great Radiance"). At that time, these two bodhisattvas arrived at the place where the Buddha was.
Having previously prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet,
he knelt with palms joined and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
beyond this point lie hundreds of thousands of billions of koṭis of buddha-fields."
The world is named Flower Accumulation (*Puṣpasaṃcaya*).
Its Buddha is named Supreme Heavenly King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
He is currently present there and has sent me to inquire after the World-Honored One’s health.
When they preach the Dharma, those who receive it with tranquility will all advance without any obstacles.
They shall not be harmed by devas, nāgas, yakṣas,
or ghosts and spirits— whether they be piśācas or kumbhāṇḍas.
If one is harassed or harmed by rākṣasas, ghosts, spirits, tigers, wolves,
or by humans or non-humans, that Tathāgata of the world [will protect them].
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has now sent me to bring this dhāraṇī bowl. For the sake of all beings,
he desires that they be brought to peace and security.
He will have a far-reaching reputation and a handsome appearance;
he will possess vitality, physical strength, and such great power as this:
*śāli mahāśāli śālani ucciṭiṃba tripadī mahātripadī*. At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
You have received this dhāraṇī-pātra; you should maintain, recite, and read it.
It is extremely difficult to encounter a Buddha, a World-Honored One;
likewise, it is also difficult to hear this dhāraṇī-pātra.
If a son or daughter of good family receives,
maintains, recites, and studies [this], they will know their own past lives for seven generations.
If a son or daughter of good family...
If one receives, maintains, recites,
and reads [this], no ghosts, spirits, humans, non-humans, snakes, vipers, adders,
or scorpions shall be able to cause harm.
Poisons cannot strike them;
sorcery shall not prevail;
they shall not be harmed by weapons of war.
The sovereign could not find an opportunity [to harm him],
yet Brahmā did not feel resentment toward him. It was thus, Ānanda.
This dharani-bowl was spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas.
If there were anyone who caused harm to it,
the words of these Buddhas would not have been otherwise.
The Bodhisattva Ajita, whose name is Maitreya,
addressed the venerable Ānanda, saying:
"I, too, shall further proclaim the dhāraṇī-pāṭha."
Why is this? It is because he also desires to bring peace and security to all,
and for his fame and virtue to be heard far and wide.
His physical appearance was upright and handsome,
and his beneficial power was such that his muscular strength was likewise great. *Aṭṭa vāṭṭa mecchakali lecchi lālami lūlami heḷi meḷi teḷi.* At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
You should receive this dhāraṇī-pātra and maintain it through recitation and study.
It is extremely difficult to encounter a Buddha, a World-Honored One;
likewise, it is also difficult to hear this dhāraṇī-pātra.
If a son or daughter of good family receives this dhāraṇī-pātra, upholds it, recites it, and reads it,
they will recognize fourteen lifetimes of their past existence.
If good sons or good daughters uphold the *dhāraṇī-bhājana*, recite it, chant it, and explain it,
they shall never be harassed or disturbed by any ghosts, spirits, humans, or non-humans.
Snakes, vipers, and all venomous insects cannot harm them;
poison cannot take effect upon them,
and sorcery shall have no power over them.
Weapons cannot harm them;
emperors and kings cannot find an opportunity to exploit them.
They are protected by Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
Ānanda, this is the dhāraṇī-pātra spoken by eighty-four thousand billion Buddhas.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
I also wish to further explain the dhāraṇī-pāṭha,
desiring to bring peace and security to all,
so that their fame and virtue may be heard afar.
His appearance was upright and handsome, and he possessed great physical strength;
his muscular power was such as this: Aṭa, Vaṭa, Neṭa, Kuneṭa, Teli, Chorapāti, Anāpāti, Panāpāti, Kacchānī, Mahākacchānī. At that time, the Buddha addressed the venerable Ānanda, saying:
Receive this dhāraṇī-pātra;
uphold, recite, and read it, and explain it extensively for the sake of all.
If there are good sons or good daughters, [who do so...]
Having received this dhāraṇī-pātra, one should uphold, recite, and read it;
thereby, one will know the infinite births of past lives.
This is the dhāraṇī-pātra.
Ānanda, this has been taught by immeasurable billions of Buddhas.
Thus, Ānanda, this is the dhāraṇī-pātra.
Whether one is traveling on a journey, or encountering thieves, or tigers and wolves—
Whether one is in the water or has committed an offense against the Emperor,
a local official, or government authorities, one should mindfully recite, chant, read,
and uphold this dhāraṇī-pāda. This is the dhāraṇī-pāda.
Ānanda, if a withered tree is bound [with this mantra], it will immediately sprout leaves, flowers, and fruit;
how much more so for one who speaks of illness on behalf of others—it shall not fail to heal.
One should therefore recite the mantra for the sake of all sick people.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the venerable Ānanda and all those in the assembly received it with joy and put it into practice.
The Sūtra on the Dharani-bhājana Spoken by the Buddha.
